source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
The manual divides corn's growth cycle into five stages, defined by growth pattern, plant-part development, and physical change in the corn plant:

Stage 1 - from planting until the seedling emerges (ចាប់ពីពេលដាំហូតដល់ពន្ដុកស្លឹក): counted from sowing until the seedling has grown 2 to 3 leaves above the soil surface. This stage lasts about 7 to 10 days after planting.

Stage 2 - from seedling establishment until tasseling (ពន្ដុកស្លឹកហូតដល់ពេលចេញផ្កា): this stage has two sub-phases -- first, growth in the number of nodes and leaves; second, elongation of the stem/internodes leading up to tassel emergence. Counted from planting, this stage lasts to about 30 days. During this stage the stem grows very rapidly in height and shape, and the plant requires ample water and fertile soil; insufficient nutrients or water at this stage can result in fewer/weaker leaves and reduced final yield.

Stage 3 - from tasseling until silking (ពេលចេញផ្កាហូតដល់ពេលចេញផ្លែ): corn generally begins flowering (tasseling) when the plant is about 45 to 75 days old after planting. From tasseling to silk emergence takes about 21 days, and from silking to a further point takes about 28 to 35 days.

Stage 4 - ear/grain development period (ពេលលូតលាស់ផ្លែ): this stage (during which the ear and kernels fill out) is named in the source but its detailed description was not clearly legible in the scanned page and is not reproduced here to avoid guessing.

Stage 5 - grain maturity (ពេលទុំ): maturity is recognized when the plant begins turning yellow, the leaves begin to wither/dry, and the moisture content in the kernel has dropped to only about 25%. A dark/brown coloring appears at the base of the kernel (associated with the kernel's black-layer/attachment point) as a maturity indicator. Counting from the day of planting to the day of maturity takes about 90 to 130 days, depending on the variety.
